messages.subject: calculate bivariate normal cumulative probability
parts:
Dear developers:

Is there any way to calculate bivariate normal cumulative probability in Stan model?

Thank you!

kk

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] calculate bivariate normal cumulative probability
parts:
Stan doesn't have any multivariate cdfs, even for bivariate normal.
And it doesn't look like there's a simple way to express it. And
it looks tricky getting it with reasonable accuracy.

It's not on our short-term to-do list, but given a C++ implementation
with tests, it would be pretty easy to add.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] calculate bivariate normal cumulative probability
parts:
I meant that if you could write an appropriate C++,
we could add it to Stan itself (appropriate means that
it has templates for all the double-type parameters and
that it has error checking and unit tests; lots of examples
in the Stan code itself).

It looks like Genz's MATLAB function implementation is under
new BSD. His R package is GPL-ed, which is too restrictive
to go into the core of Stan (we're maintaining new BSD for Stan).

There's not a good way of writing Stan extensions without
modifying the Stan code. There are some hints on how to do
that here:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Contributing-New-Functions-to-Stan

A mechanism for user-defined extensions along the lines of
that used by Eigen is on our short-term to-do list. And when
we do that, we'll doc it more thoroughly.

There's also this paper:

http://www.jstatsoft.org/v52/i10/paper

- Bob
